question: Should OpenClaw core own a new global behavior-policy and external-validator contract, or should this capability compose through existing trusted tool and message hooks as a plugin?
rationale: This choice defines a permanent security, compatibility, configuration, and availability boundary; implementation repair cannot safely choose it on behalf of maintainers.

options.title: Use plugin hooks
options.body: Keep core unchanged and implement governance through trusted tool policies plus prompt, output, and message hooks, adding only a narrowly proven missing hook if necessary.

options.title: Sponsor core policy
options.body: Approve a core framework only with a canonical schema, complete delivery and tool-interception design, upgrade semantics, and live end-to-end proof.

options.title: Pause the proposal
options.body: Defer the branch until a maintainer-sponsored threat model and ownership plan exists.

recommendation.title: Use plugin hooks
recommendation.body: Keep core unchanged and implement governance through trusted tool policies plus prompt, output, and message hooks, adding only a narrowly proven missing hook if necessary.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent agent-runtime integration work makes this person the strongest available routing candidate for the core ownership decision.
